questions: Should the cleaning step remove all non-alphanumeric characters and replace them with a space, or should it remove them entirely (i.e., concatenate adjacent characters)?

After cleaning, if the text becomes empty (e.g., only non-alphanumeric characters), what should the cosine similarity be? The reference uses denominator check, but is 0.0 always correct for empty vectors?
For cosine similarity, should term frequencies be based on raw counts (as in reference) or normalized (e.g., TF-IDF)?
Should the Levenshtein ratio be computed on the original texts or the cleaned/lowercased texts?
When splitting by spaces for word frequencies, should consecutive spaces (resulting from cleaning) produce empty strings that are filtered out?
Is the cosine similarity intended to be computed on the set of unique words from the entire corpus (both texts) or just the words present in each text?
Should the function handle non-string inputs (e.g., numbers, None) or assume inputs are strings?
If both texts are identical after cleaning, but contain no alphanumeric characters (e.g., only punctuation), should the Levenshtein ratio be 1.0 (identical empty strings) or something else?
